sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the western residential side of Paulsboro, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 19 degrees on the page so that the streets run square to its edges. West Buck Street crosses the top, West Broad Street the middle and West Thompson Avenue the lower part, with North and South Pine Street running down the centre and Paul Avenue on the left. North and South Spruce Street form the right margin, where the map continues on sheet 3. The blocks are almost entirely frame dwellings, many of two or two and a half storeys, with small sheds and outbuildings behind them on narrow lots numbered along the streets from 100 to 240. The large open lot at the upper left, with the Paulsboro Masonic Club building and the sheet's north arrow, is mostly undivided ground. A few buildings are marked as iron-clad or cement block, and a small number are shown in blue. Four-inch and eight-inch water pipes are lettered in the streets and fire hydrants stand at several corners. In the lower right the diagonal line of Swedesboro Avenue crosses the corner, with dwellings built along its north side at an angle to the grid. Margin notes refer to the adjoining sheets 5 above, 3 to the right and 21 to the left and below.
notes: Printed West Thompson Avenue is Thomson Avenue today (OpenStreetMap); North and South Pine are Pine Street, North and South Spruce are Spruce Street, West Buck and West Broad are West Buck Street and West Broad Street.
Pine Street / West Broad Street was detected about 10 m from its modern node and rejected by the fit.
50 ft; W. Buck, W. Broad, W. Thompson Av, N./S. Pine, Paul Av, N./S. Spruce; Masonic Club; one part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the centre of Paulsboro at 50 feet to an inch, turned about 19 degrees on the page. Delaware Avenue runs from the top of the sheet to the bottom, with the Swedesboro Avenue diagonal branching south-west from its junction with West and East Broad Street. West and East Buck Street cross the top, West and East Broad Street the middle, and West and East Wood Street and West and East New Street the lower part. North Spruce Street bounds the left side and the narrow North and South Chestnut Alley the right. This is the commercial core. Along North Delaware Avenue stand rows of stores, a bake shop with ovens, a plumber and a cement block one-store building, and south of Broad Street the Borough Hall with a private garage and auto sales rooms. East of Delaware Avenue are a garage with a capacity of 20 cars, a storage shed, a movie house and the Bailey Building with a light factory, a bank and a second garage with offices and a shop. St. Paul's M.E. Church stands on East Broad Street beside a large cemetery that fills the block down to East Wood Street. Near the bottom a large cement block auto repair garage holds a block on South Delaware Avenue, and the Paulsboro Vol. Fire Association No. 1 house lies on the left. Water pipes, hydrants and block numbers 87 to 103 are shown, and sheets 2, 4, 6, 19 and 21 adjoin.
notes: Printed Thompson Avenue is Thomson Avenue today (OpenStreetMap); North and South Delaware Avenue are North Delaware Street and South Delaware Street, and the Spruce streets are Spruce Street.

The modern node where Swedesboro Avenue, Thomson Avenue and West Wood Street meet does not match the drawn junctions (Thompson Avenue and West Wood meet Swedesboro Avenue at separate points), so it was excluded; so was the Spruce / Swedesboro / West New node.
Borough Hall, St. Paul's M.E. Church, a cemetery and the Paulsboro Vol. Fire Association No. 1 are lettered on the sheet.

50 ft; downtown, N./S. Delaware Av, Swedesboro Av diagonal, Buck to New; Borough Hall, St. Paul's M.E. Church, cemetery; one part. Spruce/Swedesboro/New and Swedesboro/Thomson/Wood nodes excluded (drawn junctions differ).

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the east side of the Paulsboro business district out to Great Mantua Creek, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 20 degrees on the page. North and South Commerce Street run down the sheet and jog sideways at East Broad Street, which crosses the middle and leads east over an iron bridge on to the West Deptford side of the creek. East Buck Street crosses near the top and East Wood and East New Street the lower left. West Chestnut Street and the Chestnut alleys form the left margin where the map joins sheet 3. On the left blocks 88 to 103 hold dwellings, a hay, grain and cement ware house, a lumber and planing mill office, a garage with capacity for 40 cars and an auto showroom and garage built of cement block with steel frame at the corner of East Broad Street, with a printing shop beside it. East of North Commerce Street the E. G. Miller Lumber Co. fills the creek bank with a lumber shed, a line of connected warehouses, open lumber piles, a lime and cement ware house and a coal yard; the hotel stands at the corner of East Broad Street. South of East Broad Street a boat builder with a gasoline engine, a tool house and a few dwellings lie on the creek bank. Across the iron bridge a row of seventeen numbered dwellings follows the west bank, beside a notation that the borough limits and the township line run down the middle of the creek. An oil pump house, oil tanks and a notation of no exposure appear at the right edge.
notes: East Buck, East Broad, East Wood and East New are East Buck Street, East Broad Street, East Wood Street and East New Street today; North and South Commerce are North Commerce Street and South Commerce Street (OpenStreetMap).
North Commerce Street is drawn about 35 m east of South Commerce Street at East Broad Street, a jog the modern street data also has.
A line marking borough limits and W. Deptford Township runs down the middle of Great Mantua Creek.
The map shows E. G. Miller Lumber Co. on the creek bank.
50 ft; N./S. Commerce (jog at E. Broad), E. Buck to E. New, iron bridge over Great Mantua Creek, E. G. Miller Lumber Co.; one part. No control on the creek side.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the north-west part of Paulsboro at 50 feet to an inch, turned about 19 degrees on the page. North Spruce Street forms the right margin and North Pine Street runs down the lower middle, crossed from top to bottom by West Monroe, West Madison, West Jefferson, West Adams, West Washington and West Buck Street. In the upper left the grid gives way to diagonal streets: Penn Line Road runs up the left edge, McCorkell Avenue and West Jefferson Street cross the upper centre on a slant, and Hoffman Avenue joins them from the lower left. A short street lettered Not Named runs between West Jefferson Street and the grid near the middle. The blocks, numbered 58 to 80, are almost all frame dwellings on long narrow lots, with small outbuildings and a few sheds and coops. In the lower middle, between West Adams and West Washington Street, the dwellings stand in regular rows facing each street. A cement block garage and several dwellings of cement block are shown in blue, and a bakery with an oven is marked at the upper right near West Madison Street. A part of the sheet's upper margin carries the borough's key numbers 8 and 21, indicating the adjoining sheets, with sheet 6 at the right and sheet 2 below. Water pipes and hydrants are marked along the streets.
notes: Printed McCorkell Avenue is McCorkle Avenue today (OpenStreetMap); West Monroe, Madison, Jefferson, Adams, Washington and Buck are West Monroe Street, West Madison Avenue, West Jefferson Street, West Adams Street, West Washington Street and West Buck Street; North Pine and North Spruce are Pine Street and Spruce Street.
Hoffman Avenue / West Jefferson Street, Hoffman Avenue / West Adams Street and Hoffman Avenue / McCorkle Avenue were found by the detector and fit within 0.7 m.
A short street between West Jefferson Street and the grid is lettered "Not Named".
50 ft; W. Monroe to W. Buck, N. Pine, N. Spruce, Penn Line Rd, McCorkell and Hoffman Avs; one part.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers six blocks of central Paulsboro north of the business district, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 20 degrees on the page so that the streets run square to its edges. It is bounded by West and East Monroe Street at the top, West and East Buck Street at the bottom, North Spruce Street on the left and North Chestnut Street on the right, with North Delaware Street running down the middle and West and East Madison, Jefferson, Adams and Washington crossing it. The blocks are mostly frame dwellings and stores on narrow lots, numbered 54 to 82 on the key. Along the east side of North Delaware Street between Monroe and Madison are the Post Office, a bake shop with an oven and a row of stores; on West Monroe Street a concrete block wood working shop and a small bottling works stand in block 57. A public school occupies the east side of Delaware Street above Buck Street. Four-inch and eight-inch water pipes are marked in the streets and fire hydrants at the corners. In the top right corner the tracks of a railroad cross the sheet diagonally, with Beacon Avenue lettered where it crosses them north of East Monroe Street. Margin notes refer the adjoining ground to sheets 3, 5, 7, 8 and 9.
notes: Streets are printed without suffixes; today they are West/East Monroe Street, West/East Madison Avenue, West/East Jefferson Street, West/East Adams Street, West/East Washington Street, West/East Buck Street, Spruce Street, North Delaware Street and North/South Chestnut Street (OpenStreetMap).

Pilot. W./E. Monroe to W./E. Buck, N. Spruce to N. Chestnut, N. Delaware down the middle; Post Office, public school; one part, 50 ft. Rotation about 20 degrees. E. Buck / S. Chestnut excluded (3.9 m; 5.4 m apart from sheet 3's measurement).

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the north-east side of Paulsboro at 50 feet to an inch, turned about 19 degrees on the page. North Chestnut Street bounds the left side and North Commerce Street runs down the centre, crossed by East Monroe, East Madison, East Jefferson, East Adams, East Washington and East Buck Street. A street lettered Water runs along the right side of the block near the creek. The Pennsylvania Railroad enters at the upper left and crosses the sheet diagonally in several tracks, with the P.R.R. Freight House and its platform beside the tracks and the Jos. J. Feger coal yard and G. M. Hannold, Coal, Wood and Coke, with a coal pile, on the south side of the right of way. The left half of the sheet is closely built with frame dwellings on narrow lots, blocks 62, 70 and 76 to 83. St. James Episcopal Church, a cement block building, stands on the east side of North Commerce Street near the railroad. Large open blocks east of North Commerce Street, 71 and 77, hold only a few dwellings, a storage building, a greenhouse and a stable before Great Mantua Creek, whose west bank bends down the right side. A boat repair shop sits on the bank at the upper right. At the bottom the E. G. Miller Lumber Co. planing mill and its lumber shed and open piles continue on to sheet 4. Water mains and hydrants are lettered in the streets, and margin notes refer to sheets 4, 6, 9 and 10.
notes: East Monroe, East Madison, East Jefferson, East Adams, East Washington and East Buck are East Monroe Street, East Madison Avenue, East Jefferson Street, East Adams Street, East Washington Street and East Buck Street today; North Chestnut and North Commerce are North Chestnut Street and North Commerce Street (OpenStreetMap).
Water Street is not in the modern street data.
East Buck Street / South Chestnut Street fell 3.5 m from the others and was excluded; East Washington Street / North Commerce Street was detected on the wrong line and rejected.
The railroad at the top is the line modern OpenStreetMap calls Penns Grove Secondary.
50 ft; E. Madison to E. Buck, N. Chestnut, N. Commerce, P.R.R. across the top; one part. E. Buck / S. Chestnut excluded (3.5 m).

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the northwest edge of Paulsboro, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 19 degrees on the page so that North Delaware Street runs down the right-hand side. The map lies between the borough limits, which cross the left side as a dash-dot line separating Paulsboro from Greenwich Township, and North Delaware Street. Capitol Street and Roosevelt Avenue run down to the right from the borough line to Delaware Street, with blocks 47, 48 and 49 between them, and West Quincy Street is drawn at the foot of the sheet beside a siren on a tower. The blocks are almost entirely frame dwellings with outbuildings on long narrow lots, and several of the dwellings near Delaware Street are brick or concrete block. The Paulsboro High School stands in block 47 at the top, a pink brick and fireproof building with a manual training room, heated by hot air and lighted by gas and electricity. A bank and store with a vulcanizing shop and a concrete block cement-floored works making concrete blocks stand in the blocks beside Delaware Street. The tracks of the Pennsylvania Railroad cross the lower part of the sheet from left to right, with a 50,000 gallon steel water tank on a platform beside them. Below the tracks West Monroe Street is drawn along the bottom edge, with a lumber storage yard, dwellings and a row of stores and dwellings in blocks 58 and 59; Moreland Avenue appears at the lower left beside the margin number 21. Four-inch and eight-inch water pipes are marked in the streets. The Paulsboro oval stamp, dated January 1927, appears at the top. Margin numbers refer the ground beyond to sheets 5, 6, 9, 11 and 21.
notes: Roosevelt Avenue is Roosevelt Street today (OpenStreetMap); West Monroe is West Monroe Street and North Delaware is North Delaware Street; West Quincy has no modern street west of Delaware (Quincy Street lies east of it).
The borough limits are drawn as a dash-dot line along the left side; it follows modern Penn Line Road, where Capitol Street ends.
The scale bar reads 0 to 150 feet and matches a fitted 7.96 pixels per foot, i.e. 50 feet to an inch.

50 ft; Capitol, Roosevelt Av, W. Quincy west of N. Delaware; borough line on the left; P.R.R. across the bottom; Paulsboro High School; one part. Control mostly along N. Delaware plus one hand-picked point at the borough line.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 shows the northern part of central Paulsboro at 50 feet to an inch, with north close to the top of the page. Billings Avenue and Beacon Avenue run down the sheet and are crossed by 7th Street near the top and by the narrow East Quincy Street lower down; Greenwich Avenue and North Delaware Street, which drift diagonally down the left side, and Mantua Avenue and Commerce Street on the right complete the frame, with blocks numbered 42, 43, 44, 50, 51 and 52. The blocks are mostly frame dwellings with rear outbuildings on narrow lots, with a few tile-roofed buildings near 7th Street. Churches are named on the sheet: the Taylor Memorial Baptist Church beside Greenwich Avenue, St. John's R.C. Church beside Mantua Avenue and the 1st Presbyterian Church on Billings Avenue above East Quincy Street. Block 157 between East Quincy Street and the railroad is undivided open ground. In the lower right the J. Howard Coombs lumber yard, with a planing mill, lumber sheds and scattered lumber piles, adjoins a hardware store; below it the Pennsylvania Railroad main tracks and a fan of sidings pass the railroad passenger station, and East Monroe Street is lettered at the bottom edge. A compass rose with a north arrow stands on block 52 at the right. Six-inch and eight-inch water pipes run in the streets, with fire hydrants at the corners, and a fire alarm siren on a tower is marked at the lower left beside West Quincy Street. The Paulsboro oval stamp is dated January 1927. The left edge, with Capitol Street and Roosevelt Avenue, repeats the ground of sheet 8.
notes: Modern names (OpenStreetMap): Roosevelt Avenue is Roosevelt Street; East Quincy Street is Quincy Street; Commerce is North Commerce Street; North Delaware is North Delaware Street.
West Quincy Street, drawn west of North Delaware Street, has no modern equivalent.
The scale bar reads 0 to 150 feet and matches the fitted scale of 8.04 pixels per foot, i.e. 50 feet to an inch.
50 ft; 7th St to E. Monroe; Greenwich, Billings, Beacon, Mantua Avs, E. Quincy; P.R.R. passenger station and Coombs lumber yard at the bottom; one part.

sheet-10-1.description: The main part of sheet 10, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north straight up the page, shows the works of the Sandura Co., Inc., felt base floor covering manufacturers, on the west bank of Great Mantua Creek at the northeast edge of Paulsboro. On the left, Mantua Avenue comes down from the top with frame dwellings on its east side, numbers 611 to 645, and runs into North Commerce Street, which leaves at the bottom; the tracks of the Pennsylvania Railroad cross the lower part of the sheet with a spur curving up into the works, and East Monroe Street appears at the lower left beside block 52. The works fill block 45: a long range of drying buildings with concrete floors, a festoon drying rack, paper storage, a lacquering room, coating room and print room, built of brick and concrete block, with a paint mixing building, a tube room, block cutting and storage buildings, raw linseed oil and varnoline storage tanks, a coal pile, a carpenter shop and a machine shop. A covered walk leads north to oil storage and a platform near the creek. South of the works stand an examining building, a large concrete block storage building, the office, a time office, a laboratory, a commissary with storage, and company apartments lettered A to C. A long note describes the watchman, heating, power, sprinklers, water supply pumped from the creek and the works fire brigade. A divided strip on the left and a box at the top right, drawn separately, belong to Mantua Avenue and Dupont Avenue further north.
notes: Placed by a two-point fit: the crossing of Mantua Avenue and the Paulsboro Industrial Track (detected) and North Commerce Street at the main tracks, carried from sheet 7; the fitted scale (8.03 px/ft) agrees with the 50 ft sheets. Low to medium confidence.
East Monroe Street is drawn running east to North Commerce Street; today it ends at North Chestnut Street.

Three parts divided by heavy lines, 50 ft. Part 1 (main): Sandura Co. felt base floor covering works on Great Mantua Creek, Mantua Av, N. Commerce, E. Monroe, P.R.R.; placed from a detected rail crossing of Mantua Av and a point carried from sheet 7. Part 2: strip along the east side of Mantua Av (nos. 541 to 609, block 45), placed from points carried from sheets 15 and 12 (fit 8.51 px/ft, 6 percent off; low confidence). Part 3: box at top right, Dupont Av nos. 391 to 402, anchored on two points carried from sheet 15 with the scale and rotation of sheet 15 (low confidence).

sheet-10-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 10 is a narrow strip at the left of the sheet, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and set off from the main map by a heavy line. It carries the east side of Mantua Avenue, lettered along the left edge, from the foot of sheet 15 down to about 6th Street and a little beyond, house numbers 541 to 609, all in block 45. The other side of the avenue is drawn on sheet 12, and the strip continues at the top of the main part of this sheet, where the numbers run on from 611. The lots are deep and mostly open. Near the top stands a machine shop of concrete block with a concrete floor, with small storage sheds behind it; further down are a shed and a scatter of one-storey and one-and-a-half and two-storey frame dwellings with their private garages, set near the avenue. A water pipe and a hydrant are marked in the avenue opposite 6th Street. Along the right edge of the strip run the lines of a vacant railroad right-of-way. The strip has its own north arrow, turned a few degrees from the main part's, and is drawn square to the avenue as sheets 12 and 15 are.
notes: Placed from two points carried from neighbouring sheets: the east line of Mantua Avenue at the strip's top lot line (from sheet 15) and the water-pipe junction at 6th Street (from sheet 12). The two-point fit gives 8.51 px/ft, about 6 percent larger than the 50 ft sheets: either the strip is drawn long or one of the two points is misidentified; at the atlas scale the two points disagree by about 13 m. Low confidence.
The strip's foot overlaps the top of the main part by about 9 m on the ground.

Three parts divided by heavy lines, 50 ft. Part 1 (main): Sandura Co. felt base floor covering works on Great Mantua Creek, Mantua Av, N. Commerce, E. Monroe, P.R.R.; placed from a detected rail crossing of Mantua Av and a point carried from sheet 7. Part 2: strip along the east side of Mantua Av (nos. 541 to 609, block 45), placed from points carried from sheets 15 and 12 (fit 8.51 px/ft, 6 percent off; low confidence). Part 3: box at top right, Dupont Av nos. 391 to 402, anchored on two points carried from sheet 15 with the scale and rotation of sheet 15 (low confidence).

sheet-10-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 10 is a framed box at the top of the sheet, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, turned a few degrees as on sheet 15. It shows Dupont Avenue, lettered down the middle with a 4-inch water pipe, between sheet 20 to the west and sheet 15 to the south, where the avenue continues. Dwellings stand on both sides: two-storey frame double houses numbered 392 to 402 on the west side and 391 to 401 on the east, each with a private garage. The numbers 150 (25) and 156 are lettered west and east of the houses. The lots west of the houses run back toward sheet 20 and are otherwise empty, apart from a garage. At the foot of the box a dwelling is cut by the frame; it is drawn whole at the top of sheet 15. The rest of the box is open lots.
notes: Placed from two points carried from sheet 15 (the lot line and front corner of the dwelling cut by the foot of the box), with the scale of the 50 ft sheets (8.05 px/ft) and the rotation of sheet 15 (-6.4 degrees); the second point agrees with the anchored fit to 0.2 m. Low confidence away from the foot of the box.

Three parts divided by heavy lines, 50 ft. Part 1 (main): Sandura Co. felt base floor covering works on Great Mantua Creek, Mantua Av, N. Commerce, E. Monroe, P.R.R.; placed from a detected rail crossing of Mantua Av and a point carried from sheet 7. Part 2: strip along the east side of Mantua Av (nos. 541 to 609, block 45), placed from points carried from sheets 15 and 12 (fit 8.51 px/ft, 6 percent off; low confidence). Part 3: box at top right, Dupont Av nos. 391 to 402, anchored on two points carried from sheet 15 with the scale and rotation of sheet 15 (low confidence).

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers the northwest edge of Paulsboro at 50 feet to an inch, turned about 6 degrees so that 6th Street runs across the page. North Delaware Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally from upper left to lower right, with the borough limits against Greenwich Township running down the left side as a dash-dot line. Nassau Avenue runs down the upper right and 6th Street across the middle of the right half to Greenwich Avenue at the right edge; Lincoln Avenue enters at the top, and the streets Taylor, Polk and Tyler run up to the right from Delaware Avenue as long, sloping blocks of narrow lots. Block 41 below 6th Street, blocks 33 and 34 at the top and block 47 at the foot are numbered. The Paulsboro Water Company works stands at the top beside Lincoln Avenue, a pumping plant with two 8-inch wells, three pumps of 300 and 600 gallons and a standpipe of 12 by 100 feet holding 85,000 gallons, said to operate day and night. Most of the remaining ground is frame dwellings with outbuildings, with a milk dairy on the long lots between Polk and Tyler Streets. Polk is marked as not opened. The left third of the sheet and the lower left corner are blank, belonging to Greenwich Township; a compass rose with a north arrow and the scale of feet sit there. Six-inch and eight-inch water pipes are marked in the streets. The Paulsboro oval stamp, dated January 1927, is at the top, and margin numbers refer the adjoining ground to sheets 12, 13, 14 and 21.
notes: Modern names (OpenStreetMap): North Delaware Avenue is North Delaware Street; Taylor, Tyler and Lincoln are Taylor Street, Tyler Street and Lincoln Avenue; Polk was never opened and has no modern street.
The borough limits against Greenwich Township are lettered along the dash-dot line on the left.
The scale bar reads 0 to 150 feet and matches the fitted scale of 8.06 pixels per foot, i.e. 50 feet to an inch.
50 ft; 6th St, Nassau, Lincoln, Greenwich Avs, N. Delaware Av diagonal, Taylor, Polk (not opened), Tyler; Paulsboro Water Co.; one part.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers a residential strip of northern Paulsboro at 50 feet to an inch, with the page turned only a few degrees from the streets. Greenwich Avenue runs down the left edge, followed by Billings Avenue, Beacon Avenue and Mantua Avenue at the right edge, so that four parallel avenues enclose three columns of long north-south blocks. 6th Street is the only cross street drawn; it runs across the middle of the sheet with a six-inch water main and, towards the right, a four-inch main, and the blocks above and below it are subdivided by unnamed lot lines into narrow lots. Blocks 37, 38 and 39 lie above 6th Street and 42, 43 and 44 below it, with the number 9 at the foot of the sheet marking the adjoining map. Nearly every building is a frame dwelling with a rear outbuilding, drawn as a small yellow rectangle with a cross for the porch; a few are marked concrete block or brick, a sheet metal shop stands in block 37 and poultry houses occupy long lots in block 43. A good deal of ground, mostly on the east side of Beacon Avenue and in the interior of block 39, is undeveloped. The Paulsboro oval stamp, dated January 1927, and a compass rose with a north arrow stand in the upper right. The scale of feet and copyright line appear at the bottom, and margin numbers refer the adjoining ground to sheets 9, 10, 11, 14 and 15.
notes: All four control points lie along 6th Street (Greenwich, Billings, Beacon and Mantua Avenues), so the placement is a similarity fit; the lot lines north and south of it rest on the fitted scale.
All five streets have the same names today (OpenStreetMap).
50 ft; only 6th St crossing Greenwich, Billings, Beacon and Mantua Avs; one part, placed by a helmert on the 6th St junctions.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the Billingsport district at the northwest corner of Paulsboro, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 7 degrees. North Delaware Avenue runs diagonally from the upper left to the lower right, with the borough limits against Greenwich Township drawn as a dash-dot line along its centre in the upper left and again in the lower left corner; Billingsport Road meets it at an angle near the left edge and runs off to the lower left. Sheridan Avenue and Lincoln Avenue run up and down the right-hand side and are crossed by 5th Street, with the long narrow blocks 26, 27, 33, 34 and 34A between them. Frame dwellings stand along Delaware Avenue and in the blocks beside Sheridan Avenue, with an apartment building of two and three storeys at the top, a pink brick tile building of apartments on 5th Street at Sheridan Avenue, and a bakery with an oven and storage buildings in block 18 at upper left. The Billingsport M.E. Church, a large building coloured blue, heated by steam and lighted by electricity, stands between Billingsport Road and Delaware Avenue near the bottom, and the Billingsport Volunteer Fire Department is housed in a building coloured blue marked C.B. in block 26. The Vacuum Oil Co. employment office and an adjoining fire-proof reinforced concrete building are drawn in brown at the left edge in Greenwich Township, with the remark that remittance is refused. A compass rose and the scale of feet are in the lower left, and the Paulsboro oval stamp appears at the top. Margin numbers 14 and 19 refer the adjoining ground to those sheets.
notes: North Delaware Avenue is North Delaware Street today and Billingsport Road is unchanged (OpenStreetMap); 5th Street, Sheridan Avenue and Lincoln Avenue also keep their names.
Hofman Avenue is probably Hoffman Avenue today, which lies to the west in Greenwich Township.

The dash-dot borough line follows the centre of Delaware Avenue and Billingsport Road at the left; the fitted points are the 5th Street junctions with Sheridan and Lincoln Avenues and the junctions of Delaware Avenue with Billingsport Road and Sheridan Avenue.
50 ft; Billingsport Rd / N. Delaware Av, Sheridan and Lincoln Avs, 5th St; Billingsport M.E. Church; Vacuum Oil Co. office in Greenwich Twp; one part.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and covers the Billingsport district of Paulsboro between 4th Street at the top and 5th Street across the middle, continuing south to the lower edge of the sheet. Lincoln, Nassau, Greenwich and Billings Avenues run down the page, with Lincoln Avenue at the left edge and Billings Avenue at the right edge. The blocks between 4th and 5th Streets are numbered 28, 29 and 30 and are almost empty, laid out in long lots with a few scattered frame dwellings; the one large building is the Billingsport Public School in the centre of block 29, a brick structure with a central corridor, concrete floors, steam heat and electric lights. South of 5th Street the blocks numbered 35, 36 and 37 are more built up, with rows of two-storey frame dwellings with porches and small outbuildings along each avenue. Streets carry 4-inch and 6-inch water pipes with hydrants, and 4th Street and 5th Street are lettered 50 feet wide. A compass rose with the north arrow stands in block 28 at the top. The north arrow and the street grid are turned slightly to the left of the page. Neighbouring sheets are numbered in the margins: 13 to the left, 15 to the right, 20 above and 11 and 12 below. The upper margin shows the date, Jan. 1927, and the town in an oval stamp.
notes: The 4th Street junctions are hand-picked: only the south side of 4th Street is drawn on this sheet, so its centre was placed half the drawn width (25 feet, as measured for 5th Street) from the block edge. The automatic detector paired the block edge with a lot line and put those points about 11 m too far south.
A 'Billingsport Public School' building stands in block 29; the school and its block are lettered on the sheet.
50 ft; 4th to 5th St, Lincoln to Billings Avs; one part. 4th St row hand-picked (detector paired the block edge with the first lot line, 7 m off).

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and shows the eastern part of the Billingsport district of Paulsboro. 4th Street runs along the top and 5th Street across the middle. Billings Avenue forms the left edge, with Beacon Avenue and Mantua Avenue running down the sheet to the right of it. The long blocks between 4th and 5th Streets, numbered 31 and 32, are almost empty, with a few frame dwellings and one larger building near the left edge. Block 25 and the blocks to its south lie between Mantua Avenue and the right edge. Dupont Avenue crosses obliquely at the upper right, running from Mantua Avenue to the right and turning up the page at the margin; on it stand a fire department hose house, lettered with its hose reel and hose, and a fire alarm ring. Below it block 45 holds a row of seven frame dwellings along Mantua Avenue. South of 5th Street blocks 38 and 39 carry rows of frame dwellings. A railroad siding curves down the right side from the upper right corner. 4-inch and 6-inch water pipes with hydrants run along most streets. The north arrow, in the right half, is turned slightly to the left. Adjoining sheets are numbered in the margins, among them 14 at the left and 12 below.
notes: 4th Street is only partly drawn at the top edge of the sheet; its centre was placed from the drawn block edge and the street width, so the 4th Street points are less certain than those on 5th Street.
A hose house of the fire department stands on Dupont Avenue near the right edge.
50 ft; 4th to 5th St, Billings to Mantua Av and Dupont Av; one part.

sheet-16-1.description: The lower part of sheet 16 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and shows the shore of the Delaware River at the northern end of Mantua Avenue in Paulsboro, below a heavy dividing line that separates it from the upper part. Along the top, just below the line, the Delaware River is lettered above the river bank, and Riverside Place runs along the shore, marked arbitrary, with lots numbered 541 to 554 on its inland side and a row of narrow lots numbered 22 to 40 on its west side. These lots are filled with small frame summer cottages and boat houses. A note states that all buildings on this sheet marked C are summer cottages. Mantua Avenue runs down the middle of the right half, 33 feet wide with a 4-inch water pipe, and meets Verga Avenue, lettered also Riverview Avenue, which runs to the right with a row of cottages on both sides, numbered 101 to 112. Lena Avenue, 30 feet wide, runs parallel to Mantua Avenue on the left, serving a block of dwellings and sheds numbered 154. The lower edge shows Riverview Avenue running across the sheet, with Beacon Avenue running south from it at the left and Mantua Avenue crossing it at the right. 'No exposure' is lettered down the right margin. The blocks are numbered 153, 154 and 155. The sheet adjoins sheet 20 at the bottom.
notes: Placed from two hand-picked points (Mantua Avenue and Beacon Avenue at Riverview Avenue) with scale and rotation taken from the sheet; low confidence.
The street printed 'Verga Av. (Riverview Av.)' east of Mantua Avenue no longer exists; today Mantua Avenue ends at Riverview Avenue.
Riverside Place is printed 'Riverside Pl.'; the abbreviation is written as Place here.

50 ft; Delaware River shore; two parts split by a heavy line. Part 1 (lower, larger): Riverview Av, Mantua Av, Beacon Av, Verga Av; part 2 (upper): Billingsport Rd / Riverview Av, Riverside and Byrom Places, "Hassau Av". Both placed from one or two points (low confidence). Part 1 is the lower (larger) part, numbered by size; part 2's hand-picked Nassau/Riverview point (printed "Hassau Av") checks its anchored fit to 3.4 m.

sheet-16-2.description: The upper part of sheet 16 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and shows the Billingsport riverfront of Paulsboro above a heavy dividing line, with the Delaware River along the top. Billingsport Road runs from the lower left up to the right and meets Riverview Avenue, which runs down the page to the right along the shore with a hydrant and a 4-inch water pipe. Byrom Place, marked arbitrary, lies in the upper left behind a row of small frame summer cottages along the river bank, numbered 1 to 8 and 102 to 109. Further right is a wharf extending out from the bank, with lots numbered 131 to 135 and a few cottages near it. Weatherby Hotel stands in the centre, near the narrow lots that fan out from Riverside Place, marked arbitrary and numbered 505 to 516; a second hotel, Ye Old Duffy Ho., stands at the right edge. At the bottom the land south of Riverview Avenue is blank except for Hassau Avenue, running up from the lower dividing line. A compass rose in the lower right shows north turned about 10 degrees clockwise from the top of the page. A note on the sheet at the left refers to sheet 19, which lies to the west. The blocks are numbered 2 and 3.
notes: Placed from one measured junction (Billingsport Road and Riverview Avenue) with scale and rotation taken from the sheet; low confidence.
The street lettered 'Hassau Av.' is printed that way; it is probably today's Nassau Avenue, which ends at Riverview Avenue.
Byrom Place and Riverside Place are printed 'Byrom Pl.' and 'Riverside Pl.'; the abbreviations are written as Place here.

50 ft; Delaware River shore; two parts split by a heavy line. Part 1 (lower, larger): Riverview Av, Mantua Av, Beacon Av, Verga Av; part 2 (upper): Billingsport Rd / Riverview Av, Riverside and Byrom Places, "Hassau Av". Both placed from one or two points (low confidence). Part 1 is the lower (larger) part, numbered by size; part 2's hand-picked Nassau/Riverview point (printed "Hassau Av") checks its anchored fit to 3.4 m.

sheet-17-2.description: This inset in the lower left corner of sheet 17, framed by a heavy line and drawn at 50 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, shows a stretch of West Jefferson Street just outside the borough, in Greenwich Township, west of Penn Line Road. West Jefferson Street, 33 feet wide with a four-inch water pipe, runs diagonally across the inset from the upper left to the lower right, where it crosses the tracks of the Pennsylvania Railroad, drawn along the bottom edge beside the dash-dot line of the borough limits. South of the street, in block 108, stand the Borough Gas Works: a concrete producer house with iron and steel trusses, a loading shed, iron purifying tanks, a crude oil tank and two iron gas holders of 50,000 and 30,000 cubic feet, with a transformer house and a small storage building near the street. The works note records no watchman and power, heat and light by steam and electricity. North of the street is block 160, empty apart from a hydrant. The margins are marked no exposure, and a note at the bottom refers the ground to the south to sheet 21. The inset is placed from one point, the street's crossing of the railroad as drawn on sheet 21, with the scale and the direction of north assumed.
notes: Placed from a single point carried from sheet 21 (West Jefferson Street at the railroad) with scale 8.04 px/ft and north 20.5 degrees assumed; low confidence in rotation.
The railroad is lettered P.R.R.; today the Paulsboro Industrial Track (OpenStreetMap).

Two parts, 50 ft. Part 1 (main): I. P. Thomas & Son Co. Mantua Point phosphate works between Thomas Av and Great Mantua Creek; no street junction, Thomas Av not in OpenStreetMap. Part 2: inset (bottom left), Borough Gas Works on W. Jefferson St in Greenwich Township, placed from one point carried from sheet 21.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: main map: I. P. Thomas & Son Co. Mantua Point phosphate works, Thomas Avenue (no street junction; Thomas Avenue and the works are gone (industrial land today) and no neighbouring sheet overlaps; needs hand-picked control from a historical aerial or a dated survey).

sheet-19-1.description: The main part of sheet 19, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers Billingsport, the northwest corner of Paulsboro on the Delaware River. It takes the right side of the sheet and a strip along the bottom, wrapping around the separately drawn south Paulsboro part with a heavy line. At the top the river shore runs diagonally, with small boat houses and a club at the ends of Byrom Place and the lanes off it. Below lie Summers Avenue (lettered also Riverview Avenue), Abram Place, Benners Avenue (also Wampus Place), Loncer Lane and the head of Billingsport Road with Riverview Avenue, Second Street and Lincoln Avenue to its east, most of them named arbitrarily by the map maker. Further south Billingsport Road runs down past Third Street to Clonmell Road, King Avenue, Hoffman Avenue and Fourth Street, marked not open, at the bottom edge. In the bottom strip Clonmell Road and North Delaware Avenue meet at the borough limits, with Greenwich Township beyond. The ground is thinly built with frame dwellings on long narrow lots, many blocks empty, and large blocks such as 151 and 166 have no buildings at all. The margins refer to sheets 4, 10, 13, 16, 20 and 21.
notes: Summers Avenue, also lettered Riverview Avenue, is today's Riverview Avenue; Riverview Avenue east of Billingsport Road keeps its name.
Loncer Lane (marked arbitrary) is on the line of today's Ferry Road; its junctions were not used.
King Avenue is today's King Street; North Delaware Avenue is North Delaware Street.
Fourth Street east of Billingsport Road is marked not open.
Byrom Place, Abram Place, Loncer Lane and Wampus Place are marked arbitrary (names given by the map maker).

100 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy L-shaped line. Part 1 (main, right side and bottom strip): Billingsport, Delaware River front, Summers Av (now Riverview Av), Benners Av, Billingsport Rd, Lincoln Av, 2nd to 4th St, Clonmell Rd, King Av, N. Delaware Av. Part 2 (upper left box): S. Delaware Av and S. Commerce south of New St, Jesup St.

sheet-19-2.description: The upper left part of sheet 19, framed by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch, shows the south end of Paulsboro along South Delaware Avenue below New Street. West and East New Street cross the top, with a Seventh Day Adventist church on West New Street; South Delaware Avenue runs down the middle of the part, lined with frame dwellings on narrow lots numbered 1514 to 1634, and Jesup Street leaves it to the west. South Commerce Street comes down from New Street on the right, with a few houses, and joins South Delaware Avenue about halfway down the part. Below that junction South Delaware Avenue continues alone past a brick row of dwellings, with Allyn Place, an arbitrary name, among the scattered houses to its west, and large blocks 106, 109, 112 and 166 are mostly empty. Small sheds marked foundry stand near South Commerce Street. On the left edge Moreland Avenue and Sewell Avenue are lettered where they run on to sheet 21, and margin notes refer to sheets 3, 4 and 21.
notes: Jesup is today's Jessup Street; South Delaware Avenue is South Delaware Street.
The drawn junction of South Commerce Street and South Delaware Avenue lies about 45 m north of today's junction; the street has been realigned there and the junction was not used.
Allyn Place is marked arbitrary.

100 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy L-shaped line. Part 1 (main, right side and bottom strip): Billingsport, Delaware River front, Summers Av (now Riverview Av), Benners Av, Billingsport Rd, Lincoln Av, 2nd to 4th St, Clonmell Rd, King Av, N. Delaware Av. Part 2 (upper left box): S. Delaware Av and S. Commerce south of New St, Jesup St.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers the northern Billingsport district of Paulsboro, from Riverview Avenue along the Delaware River shore at the top to 4th Street at the bottom. Lincoln, Nassau, Greenwich, Billings, Beacon and Mantua Avenues run down the page, crossed by 2nd, 3rd and 4th Streets; the blocks between them are numbered 5 to 15 and 20 to 24. At the upper left Billingsport Road runs diagonally down to the left past a row of small frame dwellings and meets Benners Avenue at the lower left edge of the road. Most of the sheet is sparsely built: scattered frame dwellings, mainly in blocks 12 and 13 near Greenwich and Billings Avenues and in block 22 at the bottom, with a few on Riverview Avenue and Thomas Avenue at the upper right. A large block in the centre of the right half is lettered as a United States Government Reservation, Lighthouse Station, admittance refused. Beacon Avenue is marked as not opened between the blocks above 2nd Street. Streets are lettered 50 or 60 feet wide, and the 3rd and 4th Street blocks carry 4-inch and 6-inch water pipes with hydrants. A compass rose at the upper left shows the north arrow turned slightly to the left. Neighbouring sheets 14, 16 and 19 are numbered at the margins.
notes: Beacon Avenue between 2nd Street and Riverview Avenue is lettered 'not opened' on the sheet.
A block in the centre of the right half is marked as the United States Government Reservation, Lighthouse Station.
100 ft; Billingsport north, 2nd to 4th St, Lincoln to Mantua Avs, Thomas Av; one part.

sheet-21-1.description: The main part of sheet 21, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the west side of Paulsboro from West Jefferson Street and the borough limits at the top to West Thompson Avenue at the bottom. Penn Line Road runs diagonally down the right half, crossed by West Adams, West Washington, West Buck and West Broad Streets, with McCorkell Avenue branching off near the top and Hoffman Avenue to the east. West of Penn Line Road lie Devault, Elizabeth and Huff Avenues and a drive along the western edge of the built-up blocks, with the large open block 110 south of West Broad Street. The blocks are filled with frame dwellings on narrow lots, with a few stores and sheds, and several streets carry four-inch water pipes and hydrants. At the top the Pennsylvania Railroad tracks cross West Jefferson Street along the borough limits, with Greenwich Township lettered beyond, and block 160 lies north of the street. The heavy line in the upper left divides this part from the separately drawn Swedesboro Avenue area. Margin notes refer to sheets 2, 5, 8 and 19.
notes: West Thompson Avenue is today's Thomson Avenue; McCorkell Avenue is McCorkle Avenue (OpenStreetMap).
The drawn crossing of West Jefferson Street and the railroad lies about 10 m from today's Paulsboro Industrial Track crossing and was rejected as control.

100 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy line. Part 1 (main): west Paulsboro, Penn Line Rd, W. Adams to W. Thompson Av, Devault, Elizabeth, Huff, Hoffman, McCorkell Avs. Part 2 (upper left): Swedesboro Av, S. Pine, S. Spruce, Baird, Sewell, Moreland Avs, Loudenslager School; drawn at about 18 degrees against part 1 at 12. Part 2 placed from Moreland/Spruce and two points carried from sheet 3; Swedesboro Av junctions about 16 m off (realigned) and not used.

sheet-21-2.description: The upper left part of sheet 21, framed by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, covers the Swedesboro Avenue area at the southwest edge of Paulsboro. Swedesboro Avenue runs diagonally from the lower left to West New Street at the top, crossed by South Pine Street, where the Second Baptist Church stands, and by Baird Avenue. To the right South Spruce Street runs from West New Street down to Moreland Avenue, with a row of dwellings on West New Street. Below Swedesboro Avenue the H. C. Loudenslager School, a fireproof building, stands in block 108, and the long blocks 110, 111 and 112 are laid out in narrow lots along Baird Avenue, Sewell Avenue and a second stretch of Moreland Avenue marked not opened, most of them still empty. A few frame dwellings stand near Swedesboro Avenue at the left edge, and Paul Avenue is lettered in the top corner. Margin notes refer to sheets 2, 3 and 19.
notes: Placed from the junction of Moreland Avenue and South Spruce Street and two points carried from sheet 3 (the water-pipe junction of West New Street and Swedesboro Avenue, and the block corner east of Spruce Street at West New Street). Low to medium confidence: three points, two of them close together.

Swedesboro Avenue's modern junctions (South Pine Street, Baird Avenue, West New Street) lie about 16 m from where this sheet and sheet 3 draw them; the avenue appears to have been realigned, and they were not used.
The lower Moreland Avenue is marked not opened; Sewell Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap.

100 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy line. Part 1 (main): west Paulsboro, Penn Line Rd, W. Adams to W. Thompson Av, Devault, Elizabeth, Huff, Hoffman, McCorkell Avs. Part 2 (upper left): Swedesboro Av, S. Pine, S. Spruce, Baird, Sewell, Moreland Avs, Loudenslager School; drawn at about 18 degrees against part 1 at 12. Part 2 placed from Moreland/Spruce and two points carried from sheet 3; Swedesboro Av junctions about 16 m off (realigned) and not used.
